lawRefs: KRS 141.019 (pension income exclusion of $31,110; Social Security exclusion)
header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Values hand-transcribed; sha256 is of the canonical body. Rate and deduction: Kentucky DOR 2026 withholding formula: "2026 Kentucky Standard Deduction: $3,360 / 2026 Kentucky Tax Rate: 3.5% of taxable income" (rate cut from 4% by 2025 H.B. 1; deduction up from $3,270 and adjusted annually under KRS 141.081(2)(a)). The $3,360 standard deduction is per return and is NOT doubled on a joint return (so mfj = 3360; Tax Foundation 2026 note: "Kentucky's standard deduction is not doubled for MFJ filers, but only for married filing separately"). Spouses may instead file separately on a combined return and each claim $3,360 against their own income, which is how most two-income couples file - an engine wanting that outcome should use 6,720 for couples where both spouses have income. No personal exemptions (small personal tax credits for age 65+ / blind and the low-income family size tax credit are not modeled). Starts from federal AGI. Social Security benefits are not taxed. Pension income exclusion: up to $31,110 per person of pension, annuity, IRA and other retirement-plan distributions at any age (more for certain pre-1998 government service). NOT MODELED: local occupational license (payroll / net profits) taxes levied by many Kentucky cities and counties on earned income. No capital-gains exclusion. Cross-checked against Tax Foundation, "State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets, 2026" (data as of Jan 1 2026, updated Feb 11 2026).

flags.standardDeduction.mfj: simplified: $3,360 on a true joint return; spouses filing separately on a combined return each get $3,360 (effective $6,720 when both have income)
flags.retirementIncomeExclusion: simplified: $31,110 per person at any age; larger exclusion for certain pre-1998 federal / state / local government service
